The compressor was designed to achieve a pressure ratio of 6:1 and a flow rate of 2 lb/sec.
An operating speed of 75,000 rpm was selected for the conventional impeller configuration.
The preliminary design found the tandem-bladed impeller offered 0.44 points higher efficiency than the conventional impeller.
The inducer section was designed to limit the diffusion factor to 0.5 and the static pressure rise coefficient to 0.55.
The final tandem impeller design had an estimated adiabatic efficiency of 0.8774.
Provisions were made to withdraw a portion of the boundary layer fluid to inhibit or eliminate potential flow separation issues.
The impeller tip speed was 1162 ft/sec.
The inducer had 19 blades, and the impeller had 19 blades plus 19 splitter vanes.
The corrected flow per unit frontal area was estimated to be 29.1 lb/ft^2-sec.
The preliminary design evaluated radial and backward-curved impellers, both with conventional and tandem blading.
The preliminary design evaluated conventional vane diffusers, pipe diffusers, and cascade vane diffusers.
The cascade vane diffuser was ultimately selected for the detailed design.
Potential challenges included precisely matching the flow from the inducer to the impeller inlet and the effect of flow mismatch on operating range.
The tandem impeller design used standard axial flow rotor design practices for the inducer section.
The final compressor design incorporated a separate inducer and centrifugal impeller.
